newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end at record high for fourth day.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end at record high for fourth day.

text.p: Swiss shares shook off early weakness to close on Monday at a record high in both SMI and SPI indices for the fourth day in a row.
Dealers said trade was mixed as a fall in last week's high-flyer Novartis was offset by gains in other high-profile shares such as Nestle and Roche.
One trader said that despite the high levels, the general upward trend seemed likely to continue due to a favourable Wall Street, dollar exchange rates and interest rates.
The Swiss Market Index (SMI) of leading shares ended 26.0 points or 0.47 percent higher to 5,587.8 points and the broad SPI added 11.98 points or 0.34 percent to end at 3,530.10.
Bourse volume reached 2.67 billion Swiss francs.
Most-active Novartis ended down 14 francs at 2,276 after suffering from profit taking following last week's bull run spurred by a presentation last Tuesday that was well-received by analysts.
Nestle shot up 43 francs, or 2.33 percent, to 1,890. Dealers cited technical reasons for the rise as the stock broke through the resistance level around 1,859.
Roche certificates also broke through resistance around 13,350, gaining 255 francs to end at 13,500.

Roche may have profited from news the company was selling its Humacao plant in Puerto Rico and nine prescription pharmaceutical products to ICN Pharmaceuticals Inc in a deal valued at a net $145 million.
"This deal reaffirms Roche's commitment to focusing," the dealer said.
Bearer shares of watchmaker SMH slid 15 francs to 877. The stock was trading ex-dividend nine francs.
Major banks Credit Suisse and UBS ended slightly down while SBC gained one franc to 373.50.

Alusuisse registereds were up 27 francs or 1.8 percent at 1,527. Dealers said there was some speculation in the market that Alusuisse's new chief executive Sergio Marchionne may announce a major shift in strategy at a July 4 news conference.
Marchionne said in April he would continue Alusuisse's focus on three core businesses -- aluminium, chemicals and packaging.
